name: MORSE-STEM
description: Abstract Automated scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) increasingly requires a controller to choose not only where to measure, but also which measurement mode to use under a limited electron budget. This choice is objective-dependent: a policy that is effective for intensity-centred sampling may be poorly matched to a task that values detector-specific or modality-specific information. We present MORSE-STEM, a multimodal routing and scoring scheme that represents acquisition as a budgeted sequence of location–modality decisions. The approach is evaluated in an offline replay benchmark built from public UiO-66 sparse 4D-STEM scans paired with external high-angle annular dark-field scout images, giving 69 matched real scans with modality-dependent action costs. On this benchmark, controller rankings change when the reward objective is changed. Under an intensity-centred scalar reward, the myopic scalar controller gives the highest mean reward. Under a multimodal-discovery reward, the budgeted hierarchical controller gives the highest mean reward, increasing the score from 3.54 for the myopic scalar baseline to 20.27. Held-out detector analyses show that the two reward modes correspond to different endpoint families: scalar rewards track intensity-like proxies, whereas the multimodal reward emphasizes dark high-angle and imbalance-rich regions reconstructed from raw sparse event streams.
